players.product: Akamai Inference Cloud / cloud infrastructure services (CIS): distributed GPU cloud for AI inference on NVIDIA GPUs, sold on multi-year take-or-pay commitments

quarterly_data.signal: Akamai's 8-K / release: the $11.6 billion Anthropic contractual commitment over seven years adds to the more than $2.8 billion of multi-year Cloud Infrastructure Services (CIS) commitments across Akamai's customer base previously announced this year; the transaction provides for potential expansion by up to an additional $9 billion (total potential commitment approximately $20 billion). CEO Tom Leighton: Akamai's expanding global footprint positions it 'to be the infrastructure provider for secure and responsible AI applications and workloads'.
quarterly_data.figure: $11.6 billion Anthropic commitment (seven years) on top of more than $2.8 billion of 2026 CIS commitments; potential total approximately $20 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Akamai's 8-K / release: total capital expenditures related to the $11.6 billion Anthropic commitment are estimated at approximately $5.5 billion. Akamai anticipates no impact to its 2026 revenue guidance and an increase of approximately $1.7 billion in 2026 capital expenditures to secure and pre-purchase critical supply chain components, including memory.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $5.5 billion capex for the Anthropic commitment; 2026 capex up approximately $1.7 billion; 2026 revenue guidance unchanged

quarterly_data.signal: Supplier Jabil: on September 24, 2026 Akamai and Jabil entered into a Build Request under their existing Master Services Agreement (dated May 23, 2019), under which Jabil provides Akamai with contract manufacturing and related services, including the manufacture of customized server hardware and warranty, spare parts and repair services. Akamai authorized Jabil to purchase approximately $1.7 billion of memory components, with Akamai paying Jabil all corresponding supplier invoice amounts upon Jabil's receipt of the components; pending use Jabil holds the components in consignment as bailee for Akamai and repurchases them from Akamai at cost as they are utilized. Akamai determined the Jabil Agreement is a material agreement (Item 1.01).
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $1.7 billion of memory components authorized

connects_to.relationship: Dedicated cloud computing capacity and managed support services (Anthropic Master Services Agreement)

contracts.signal: On September 18, 2026 Akamai and Anthropic entered into Project Plan 2 and Project Plan 3 under their existing Master Services Agreement dated May 5, 2026, under which Akamai provides Anthropic with dedicated cloud computing capacity and related managed support services. Subject to termination rights and satisfaction of delivery and service availability requirements, Anthropic has committed to pay approximately $11.6 billion in aggregate under the Project Plans, each with an initial seven-year term from its service start date. Per the release, the commitment supports Anthropic's accelerating CPU workload demands using Akamai Cloud's distributed AI infrastructure and software.
contracts.units: dedicated cloud computing capacity (Project Plans 2 and 3)

players.product: ThinkSystem AI servers (Neptune liquid cooling) and AMD Helios racks

connects_to.relationship: Hardware products, software programs and related services (Master Product and Services Agreement)

contracts.signal: On September 23, 2026 Akamai and Lenovo (Lenovo Global Technologies Ireland International Limited) entered into a Master Product and Services Agreement and Statement of Work No. 1, under which Lenovo will provide Akamai and certain of its affiliates with hardware products, software programs and related services; the MPSA has an initial three-year term and the SOW a seven-year term. Akamai filed it as a material definitive agreement (Item 1.01).
contracts.units: hardware products, software programs and related services
